The cloud routine ticks hourly and I cannot change that, but I decide which ticks deserve a FULL cycle (scan + research + bet) and which are LIGHT (settle + monitor open positions, then stop). Set next_full_cycle_after when a full cycle would be wasted — e.g. no candidate resolves for hours, or research sources are unavailable. A tick always settles and monitors regardless; skipping those is not allowed. LIGHT ticks skip only scan+research: if resolve.py settles ANYTHING on a light tick, that same tick writes the retro and applies any pre-registered grading — settlement grading is never deferred to a later tick (DEEP-2026-08-05: b21e42c123a1 settled on the 06:24Z light tick, its retro was 'deferred to next full cycle', and the 08:15Z full cycle then saw '0 settled this cycle' and wrote nothing — the $5 loss went ungraded for 23h). A LIGHT tick that settles only forecasts still writes the retro (RETRO-20260901-2222 and RETRO-20260902-0212 both did this correctly). watch_items_comment: DEEP-2026-08-14: deferred obligations need a carrier that every tick actually reads, and this file is the only one with that property. Rule: every FULL cycle scans watch_items and acts on any item whose trigger has fired; retros add/prune items; hourly rewrites of this file MUST preserve this key. DEEP-2026-09-07 compaction rule: MTM checkpoints inside a watch item are a rolling log, not an archive -- a bare 'unchanged/flat' checkpoint REPLACES the previous bare checkpoint rather than appending; keep the first checkpoint, the latest, and any checkpoint that crossed the 0.10 call-out threshold or changed the thesis (evidence: the Sweden next-PM item reached 13 near-identical flat checkpoints, ~4KB re-read every tick, by 2026-09-07). DEEP-2026-09-08 addition: when a watch item's bet AND all its tracked siblings are settled and graded, the next deep retro replaces the item with a one-line ARCHIVED pointer (ledger id, settlement, retro file) -- the narrative stays in git history; every tick re-reads this file, and stale multi-KB items for settled bets (NFP/UR items sat 4 days claiming 'settlement pending' after both were graded) are pure re-read cost with a misleading surface.

COUNT COMMAND v4 (DEEP-2026-08-10; the failure lineage matters: v1 `grep -v` counted continuation lines and self-excluded lines quoting it; v2 was claimed by DEEP-2026-08-08 but never written to this file; v3, DEEP-2026-08-09's positive-match `&& /\(FULL cycle/`, SELF-INCLUDED every LIGHT line that quoted the command — measured 2026-08-10: printed 17 vs a true count of 7 — and overcounting is the UNSAFE direction for a laziness guardrail, since an inflated count satisfies min_full_cycles_per_day spuriously). Use exactly: awk -v c="$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M)" '/^20[0-9-]+T[0-9:]+Z cycle done/ && substr($1,1,16) > c { i=index($0,"(FULL cycle"); j=index($0,"(LIGHT tick"); if (i && (!j || i<j)) n++ } END{print n+0}' journal/cycles.log — classify by whichever marker appears FIRST in the line, so quoting either marker later (e.g. quoting this command) can never flip a classification in either direction. Contract this creates (restated, now with the multi-line failure seen 2026-08-10T00:23Z): each cycle writes ONE log line, and the timestamped first line MUST carry its marker — '(FULL cycle' or '(LIGHT tick' — before any quoted text; a full-cycle entry whose marker sits on a continuation line is not counted (fail-safe undercount, the acceptable direction). Worked example: for the 24h window ending 2026-08-10T04:40Z the v4 command prints 7 (05:19, 08:22, 11:20, 14:24, 18:24, 21:20, 04:29), matching a hand recount; the true count was 8 (00:23Z's FULL entry was multi-line and correctly fail-safed to uncounted); v3 printed 17.
